item.description:
### Signing out now really does end the protection
Kahf Guard kept enforcing after the account behind it was gone: block lists, schedules, guards and website rules all carried on, and a subscription that ended after the sign-out was never noticed. Protection now stops with the session. Nothing is deleted — your lists, schedules, habits and word lists are all still there when you sign back in.
A Mac managed by an organisation is deliberately unaffected: its protection belongs to the organisation, and ends when the organisation removes the device.
### Sign Out says what it costs before it does it
Signing out erases this Mac and returns it to setup. It now says so first, and asks. Deleting your account does the same clean-up instead of leaving a policy behind with no account to answer for it.
